name: Sèvres rococo porcelain
summary: Soft-paste porcelain of the royal factory at Sèvres. A glossy ground colour, such as bleu céleste or rose, frames white reserves that carry flowers and birds, with fine gilt edges. Louis XV and Madame de Pompadour were its patrons.

philosophy.core_thesis: A soft, glassy body takes a deep, even ground colour that no hard paste can match; the painter then leaves white windows for the flowers.
design_principles: Fire a glassy soft paste with a lead-rich glaze at about 1100 °C.
Lay a ground colour, such as a sky blue or a rose, in an even layer over the glaze.
Leave white reserves in the shape of a cartouche, and paint flowers, birds or scenes in them.
Outline each reserve with a fine band of gold, and add small gold dots and scrolls.
Model the form in curves: a double curve at the rim, a scroll handle, a shell foot.
Mark the base with two crossed L letters and a date letter, so that each piece can be dated.
Leave the figures in unglazed biscuit, with a soft, matt surface like marble.
anti_patterns: A hard white body with a dry, bright glaze
Plain white ware with no ground colour
A printed outline filled with colour
A strict straight line and a Greek key border

form.shape: Plates with a scalloped rim, tureens known as pots à oille, sauceboats with shell handles, and large cooler bowls.
form.profile: A soft double curve at the rim and a swelling body; the edge is scalloped or has a wavy moulded border.
form.foot_and_rim: A low, narrow foot ring with a glazed base; the rim is wavy, with a gilt line on the edge.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 23 to 25 cm and wall 2 to 3 mm thick; the ground colour covers about one half of the surface.
rules: Mould the border in a wavy outline with 6 or 8 scallops.
Make the reserve one third of the plate width, in the shape of a cartouche.
Gild the edge, the handle and the line of each reserve.

bodies.rule: Use a soft paste of glass frit and white clay, which fires at a lower heat than a hard paste and takes a rich ground colour. Do not use hard paste: it came to Sèvres only after 1770.

methods: slip casting of figures and vases
painting a ground colour over the glaze
forming.joins: Cast handles and flowers are luted with slip; gilt bronze mounts are fixed to large vases after the firing.
forming.details: Fine gilt lines, a date letter in a double L mark, and a painter mark in a small sign.

glaze.pattern: Flower sprays, birds, putti and garden scenes in white reserves, on grounds of sky blue, rose, apple green or yellow, with gold scroll work.
glaze.gloss: Deep, liquid gloss, about 85 to 95 GU on the glazed parts; the biscuit is matt.
glaze.wear: The gold wears first; the soft glaze can scratch, and the ground colour can craze in a fine net.

palette.strategy: A deep, flat ground colour in one tone, white reserves, soft flower colours, and gold lines.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired kiln that fires a biscuit, then a glaze; separate muffle kilns for enamel and gold.
processes: painting and firing of the reserves
gilding and a last gold firing
firing.scale: A royal factory of about 200 workers, with painters, gilders, sculptors and chemists.
firing.signs: Crossed L marks with a date letter, a painter mark, and an even, glassy ground colour.

pieces.form: Plate with a scalloped rim, a sky-blue ground and a flower reserve in the well
Pot à oille on a stand, with a rose ground, gilt scrolls and a flower knop
Shell-shaped boat with a moulded border and a gilt edge
Pierced basket dish with moulded flowers and a gilt rim

positive: bleu céleste ground with white reserve
rose ground colour and gilt scrolls

canonical_works.work: Potpourri vase in the shape of a ship (pot-pourri à vaisseau)

evidence.title: Sèvres pair of potpourri vases, Walters 48590

emotion.target_response: A light, flirtatious pleasure: the viewer sees a sky-blue ground, a few flowers and gold lines, and thinks of a court salon.

use_cases: a French court dinner service prompt
a museum label on Sèvres soft paste
avoid_when: the brief wants a strict classical form
the brief needs a hard white porcelain
the brief wants a rustic or matte look

modifiers.how: Change to a plain cream earthenware with a straight rim, and drop the ground colour and the curves.
Change to a white hard paste with a modelled relief and a full enamel palette.
Change to bone china, simplify the ground colour to a band, and keep the gold.
